messages:
deploy-bot: Canary deploy started: rollout d-2026.03.15 -> runtime-v2.1.4, traffic slice 10%
incident-bot: paging eng-oncall (priority: high). reason: canary p95 latency spike + kernel fallback detected
sam: I’m on it. grabbing logs and checking metrics. any immediate customer alerts?
maya: looking at canary nodes now. I see repeated 'kernel eviction' messages in /var/log/runtime/kernel.log on canary pods. p95 jumped from 220ms -> 1.1s in ~3m
jon: Cloudwatch: CPU on canary pods up ~40%, but GPU mem pressure is spiking and batcher reports dropping to single-token batches. suspect KV cache thrash causing fallback to slower codepath
sam: Can you paste the kernel/fallback logs?
maya: sure — snippet from one canary pod (trimmed):
```
[03-15T12:04:21Z] runtime: kernel_select: optimized_kernel_evicted id=0x7f9a2c
[03-15T12:05:03Z] runtime: batching: disabled due to mem_pressure (threshold=0.85 current=0.92)
[03-15T12:05:04Z] runtime: fallback_kernel loaded: generic_attention
[03-15T12:06:10Z] kvcache: eviction_count=273 miss_ratio=0.67
```
jon: that eviction_count and miss_ratio are huge for this workload. consistent with bucketed traffic causing cache churn
lucy: are customers impacted? any errors surfaced in API gateway?
sam: No 5xx spike, mostly latency increase. We have some SLO alerts for p95. product notified via status page draft: "We are seeing increased latency for a subset of requests; engineering is investigating."
maya: hypothesis: the new runtime-v2.1.4 contains an altered kernel scheduling heuristic; on low-fanout workloads it increases kernel footprint which interacts badly with our KV cache sizing on canary nodes
jon: mitigation options: 1) reduce canary traffic from 10% -> 2% 2) flip feature flag to force old kernel heuristic 3) rollback the canary entirely 4) increase KV cache mem on canary (risky mid-deploy)
sam: we should act fast. rollback has the highest blast radius for other things. prefer option 2 + traffic reduce, then evaluate. any objections?
lucy: agreed — try minimal impact path first. keep status updates to customers. :+1:
maya: I can flip the runtime_heuristic_v1 flag on the canary slice. command:
```
curl -X POST "https://flags.redwood.internal/api/v1/flags/flip" -H 'Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN' -d '{"flag":"runtime_heuristic_v1","scope":"canary","value":true}'
```
jon: I’ll reduce the canary traffic slice concurrently:
```
deploy-bot: update-traffic --deploy d-2026.03.15 --slice canary --percent 2
```
maya: flipping flag now.
[maya performs action]
maya: flag toggle API returned 200. Confirming on canary pods — kernel scheduling log shows heuristic=v1 at 12:08:03Z
sam: jon, reduce applied?
jon: deployed update-traffic, service reports slice at 2% at 12:08:10Z. Cloud metrics show p95 dropping already to ~480ms
lucy: nice, any other side effects?
maya: batcher still recovering but KV miss_ratio trending down to 0.42. no new eviction spikes in last 2m
sam: OK. continue monitoring for 10m, then escalate if it reappears. Notifying incident commander and product.
incident-bot: incident severity upgraded to SEV2 due to customer p95 SLO breach window.
sam: @maya @jon please keep watch. if p95 goes back above 800ms for >3m we rollback. If it stays below 500ms after 10m we can promote change as mitigation and then prepare formal rollback ticket if we end up reverting the release fully.
maya: understood. creating ticket: RUNTIME-1267 (mitigation: flag flip + traffic reduce).
jon: quick customer impact note for RM: "No 5xx errors observed. Latency spike for small subset (canary) impacted some internal tenants; mitigation applied, p95 improving."
lucy: posting brief to status page now.
[some time passes]
maya: 12:16:30Z p95 = 360ms, cluster KV miss_ratio = 0.21, no evictions in last 4m
sam: excellent. mark handoff to next on-call in 30m. preparing a short post-incident doc.
jon: FYI we should add a canary isolation test in CI that simulates KV pressure to catch this earlier. filing follow-up: ENGOPS-342
maya: also adding a safety toggle to revert kernel scheduling remotely without a full deploy.
lucy: thanks team. will update stakeholders. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: incident resolved for customer impact; monitoring mode active.
sam: closing thread after handoff. great quick mitigation everyone.
